criteria.description: Correctly identifies low variance as a consistent bottleneck/precision requirement.
Correctly identifies high variance as demonstrator freedom, and states the practical use.

solutions.fullSolution: Low variance at time t means every demonstration passed through nearly the same x_t there, indicating a genuine task requirement (precise grasp point, keyhole, etc): a consistent bottleneck. High variance indicates freedom (many paths worked equally well). This lets a downstream controller enforce precision only where it actually matters.

criteria.description: Correctly explains training loss is only evaluated at expert-visited states.
Correctly explains test-time states are determined by pi_theta itself, creating the mismatch.

solutions.fullSolution: Training loss is only ever evaluated at states the expert actually visited (all the dataset contains). At test time, pi_theta itself determines which states get visited; a small early error can reach states the expert never demonstrated, never trained on. So training loss under pi*'s distribution says nothing about loss under pi_theta's own distribution: distributional shift, absent from ordinary i.i.d. supervised learning.

criteria.description: Correctly contrasts linear scaling in epsilon vs quadratic scaling in T.
Correctly states the implication for long-horizon behavior cloning.

solutions.fullSolution: Doubling epsilon (T fixed) doubles the bound's second term, linear. Doubling T (epsilon fixed) quadruples it, since T appears squared. This means plain BC is structurally worse-suited to long-horizon tasks than short ones even with identical per-step accuracy, since small errors compound quadratically with length, motivating DAgger and other fixes for long horizons.

criteria.description: Correctly states an advantage (DAgger-friendly second stage, simple augmentation).

solutions.fullSolution: Advantage: the distillation stage can be trained cheaply with DAgger since the teacher can be queried on-demand; data augmentation is simple. Cost: simulation-focused (needs a source of privileged ground truth) and hierarchical (requires domain knowledge to design the split). Trades a harder one-stage problem for two easier stages, at the cost of needing privileged info and added complexity.

criteria.description: Correctly describes GAN and VAE's two-network structures.
Correctly describes Diffusion's single-network denoising structure.

solutions.fullSolution: GAN: two networks trained adversarially, generator (produce realistic samples) and discriminator (tell real from generated). VAE: two networks trained cooperatively, encoder (compress to latent) and decoder (reconstruct from latent), with a KL regularizer. Diffusion: one network trained to remove noise, applied repeatedly; forward noising is fixed, the single trained network learns the reverse denoising step, generating samples via iterated application starting from pure noise.
